justification: Targeted round-3 re-check of the single sentence that capped round 2 at 7.0. Round 2 flagged one factual error near line 415 ('Random's algorithm changed in .NET 6, so a reader on an older major version would see different ... numbers from the same seed' -- backwards, since seeded Random(seed) actually kept the pre-.NET-6 algorithm) and explicitly forecast that correcting this one sentence, with nothing else touched, would clear 9+. I verified three things independently rather than trusting the writer's report. (1) Diff: `git diff 8c4b90e 15a5c50 -- src/content/articles/algorithms/sorting-algorithms-compared.md` (8c4b90e = the round-2 writer pass that was reviewed and scored 7.0; 15a5c50 = the round-3 writer pass) shows exactly one changed line -- line 415 -- and nothing else in the file differs. The new sentence in the article matches the writer's claimed fix verbatim: '`Random`'s algorithm changed in .NET 6, but only for the parameterless `new Random()`; a seeded `new Random(seed)`, which is what every measurement on this page uses, deliberately kept the pre-.NET-6 algorithm for compatibility, so these numbers reproduce exactly on any .NET version from 6 onward.' (2) Primary-source verification: I fetched the live dotnet/runtime main-branch Random.cs myself. It shows `public Random() => _impl = GetType() == typeof(Random) ? new XoshiroImpl() : new CompatDerivedImpl(this);` for the parameterless constructor (comment: 'with no seed specified, if this is the base type, we can implement this however we like'), and `public Random(int Seed) => _impl = GetType() == typeof(Random) ? new CompatSeedImpl(Seed) : new CompatDerivedImpl(this, Seed);` for the seeded constructor (comment: 'with a custom seed, if this is the base Random class, we still need to respect the same algorithm that's been used in the past'). This independently confirms the corrected claim exactly: unseeded `new Random()` on the base type gets the new Xoshiro256** algorithm introduced in .NET 6; seeded `new Random(seed)` on the base type routes to `CompatSeedImpl`, the pre-.NET-6 legacy algorithm, specifically for backward compatibility. Every seeded-Random call on this page (`Random(1)`, `Random(2)`, `Random(3)`, `Random(5)`, `Random(7)`, `Random(11)`) is a bare `new Random(seed)` on the base type, not a derived subclass, so `CompatSeedImpl` applies in every case and the article's 'reproduce exactly on any .NET version from 6 onward' claim is correct as stated. (3) Regression check: ran `node tools/run-code.mjs src/content/articles/algorithms/sorting-algorithms-compared.md` from PowerShell myself and got PASS, blocks=28, executed=14, matching the expected result exactly -- no code was broken by the change (expected, since the diff touches only prose). Per the round-2 reviewer's own note that the sentence carries no inline citation, I checked: it still doesn't link a source, and Random.cs is not in the article's front-matter sources list (only ArraySortHelper.cs and Array.cs are). Round 2 treated this as secondary to the factual error itself and explicitly predicted a 9+ once the fact was corrected regardless; I'm treating it the same way here rather than reopening a new cap on a dimension round 2 did not use to cap the score, since this round's scope is the one factual fix.
